source_reports.scope: One owned standalone PIE; real shield hits, scheduled fire nut, scheduled summon and unchanged native fuses

fixture_tuning.equipment_profile_read_source: Public MCInventoryComponent.Profile; native BeginPlay loads this into its private Settings cache, with the same 40 damage fallback
fixture_tuning.reason: Initial durability and position-only staging keep the short visual clip readable; subsequent health loss is real held-primary damage

limitations: Natural F3 rain and boss entrance precede the clips; position-only dodging protects the observer.
The shield starts with four base Pickaxe hits of durability as an explicit PIE preview fixture; native default 500 is covered separately.
Both boss walking speeds and unrelated readiness clocks are isolated only in PIE; boss/projectile damage and player health stay native.
Held primary input damages the shield; no Python damage resolver or attack helper is invoked.
Crack component/clock telemetry must be paired with inspection of the genuine rendered footage.
No content saves, network, complete battle, build, cook or package.
Summon readiness and observer/review-camera positions are explicit PIE fixtures; no summon speed, health, damage, radius or fuse is changed.
Pickaxe kill is optional and attempted only at a supported isolated approach; the remaining summons must detonate naturally.
ProceduralMeshLibrary exposes vertices/triangles but no vertex colors; spark alpha and visual quality require inspection of the genuine footage.
Pulse intervals are measured from actual visual-scale peaks; inadequate sampling is reported instead of inventing acceleration evidence.

timing: Separate actual game-time windows; every written source frame is retained with its timestamp. No temporal interpolation or time scaling.
presentation: 30 fps H.264 output repeats real captures; final hold is the median requested source interval. Demux/output timing quantization is explicitly recorded.
missing_policy: Missing screenshot requests are listed, not filled with invented frames. Real intervals across missing requests are preserved.
visual_approval: Pending inspection of the actual gameplay/VFX footage; successful encoding is not visual approval.

wizard_summon.final_hold_policy: Median requested capture interval; a presentation hold, not a source timestamp.
